text:
carla-support: Hey team, flagged by CS — customer XYZ on Dedicated is seeing 0 GPUs listed in the Dedicated Capacity dashboard after yesterday's cluster rename/upgrade. They report their nodes are healthy in k8s but the console shows empty inventory.

alice-sre: Oof. Any error from the inventory service or metrics pipeline?

carla-support: I asked for screenshots and they sent the dashboard (all zero) + kubectl output showing nodes with GPU allocatable. Pasted the kubectl snippet.

carla-support: ```
$ kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable.nvidia\.com/gpu
node-a   4
node-b   4
node-c   8
```

ben-platform: Thanks. I'll check the internal inventory ingestion. Could be the node labels changed during rename and our scraper predicate missed them.

dave-dedicated: We pushed the cluster rename last night and also toggled the nodepool label scheme from `dedicated=true` -> `redwood.pool=dedicated`. Inventory job looks for the old label for now (we planned a migration).

alice-sre: That explains a label mismatch. But why did this start showing as 0 instead of stale values? Does dashboard pull live inventory or read from time-series store?

ben-platform: Dashboard reads cached inventory from inventory-service, which updates from the nodewatcher -> writes to postgres + emits metrics to metrics-ingest. If nodewatcher filter dropped nodes, inventory-service would write zero and metrics pipeline would emit zeros.

infra-bot: deployment "nodewatcher" restarted by deploy-bot at 2026-02-12T02:14:33Z

deploy-bot: rollouts/nodewatcher v3.7.1 -> v3.8.0 completed (canary 10%)

carla-support: Repro steps requested by customer: they refreshed console at ~02:30 UTC and saw zeros. They can still run inference fine, so real capacity exists.

ben-platform: Quick triage commands to check:
```
# check nodewatcher logs for label predicates
kubectl -n infra logs deployment/nodewatcher | grep "label_predicate"
# query inventory API
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://internal.inventory.redwood/v1/dedicated/pools | jq .
```

alice-sre: I'll run the log grep. If nodewatcher is filtering on old label, we need either to: 1) update nodewatcher to check both labels; 2) patch node labels back; or 3) run a one-off sync that maps old->new in inventory.

dave-dedicated: We intentionally changed labels to standardize, but forgot to ship a migration. My bad. For minimal impact, we can enable a compatibility flag in nodewatcher config that accepts `redwood.pool=dedicated` OR `dedicated=true` for 24h.

ben-platform: I see nodewatcher logs showing: "label_predicate=dedicated=true" and it is dropping nodes without that label. Also inventory-service received an empty list and wrote counts 0. Log excerpt: `INFO reconcile: selected_nodes=0 predicate_match=0`

carla-support: Customer wants ETA; their infra shows load and they have a production window. Any quick mitigation?

alice-sre: Fastest is to update nodewatcher config via k8s patch to include the new label OR make nodewatcher consult multiple labels. I'll prepare a patch and mark as temp change.

ben-platform: I can run a manual resync endpoint to repopulate inventory after nodewatcher fix: `POST /internal/inventory/v1/resync?force=true` — that'll rebuild from k8s API and postgres. Will take ~30s for small clusters.

dave-dedicated: I'll approve and apply the config patch. Patching now.

infra-bot: patch applied to deployment/nodewatcher by dave-dedicated (patch: accept_labels=["dedicated=true","redwood.pool=dedicated"])

alice-sre: nodewatcher logs now show predicate includes both labels and selected_nodes=3. Good.

ben-platform: Triggering resync now.

ben-platform: ```
$ curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://internal.inventory.redwood/internal/inventory/v1/resync?force=true -w "\\nstatus: %{http_code}\\n"
status: 202
```

carla-support: Customer confirmed in chat: dashboard updated ~15s after resync, GPUs reflect actual counts. They are happy but want postmortem and a preventative fix. :thumbsup:

alice-sre: Next steps:
- Create a small migration script to backfill label mapping in inventory DB for 48h window (ben)
- Add unit/integration test to nodewatcher for label schema compatibility (alice)
- Update runbook and alert: inventory drop -> check label predicate mismatch (carla)

dave-dedicated: I'll also schedule a follow-up to complete label migration across clusters next week so we can remove compatibility flag.

ben-platform: Creating an incident ticket and assigning owners. I'll include the resync command and logs, and link to the customer support thread.

carla-support: Thanks everyone. Customer says no billing impact, just UI visibility. Closing customer-facing ticket, keep internal incident open until migration complete.

alice-sre: Leaving this channel with action items. If anyone observes inventory anomalies in other clusters, ping #eng-platform.

ben-platform: Filing PR for nodewatcher compatibility + test: https://git.redwood/inventory/nodewatcher/pull/482

carla-support: Closing thread here. Good job.
